_note: Manual spot-check, each answer read against the Act text. A verdict only applies while the pipeline output is exactly the reviewed text (reviewed_answer + reviewed_plain_language); any change in output shows as 'unreviewed'.

T1.reviewed_answer: A child is defined as an individual who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
T1.reviewed_plain_language: Under this law, a child is anyone under eighteen years old.

T2.notes: Rewrite adds 'promptly'; 8(6) sets no timing, only 'form and manner as may be prescribed'.
T2.reviewed_answer: An organisation must give the Board and each affected Data Principal intimation of the breach in the prescribed form and manner.
T2.reviewed_plain_language: If your organization experiences a personal data breach, you must inform the Board and the affected individuals promptly, following the specific guidelines set by the government.

T3.notes: Any time; ease comparable to giving consent.
T3.reviewed_answer: Yes, you can withdraw your consent at any time, and it should be as easy as giving it.
T3.reviewed_plain_language: You can revoke your consent whenever you want, and it should be just as easy as when you first gave it.

T4.notes: Up to Rs 250 crore, Schedule item 1.
T4.reviewed_answer: The maximum fine for not taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent a data breach is two hundred and fifty crore rupees.
T4.reviewed_plain_language: If a Data Fiduciary does not take reasonable security measures to protect personal data, they could be fined up to two hundred and fifty crore rupees.

T5.notes: Content matches 5(1) but attributed to 6(10) (citation error).
T5.reviewed_answer: The notice must inform the Data Principal about the personal data to be processed, the purpose of processing, and how to exercise rights and make complaints.
T5.reviewed_plain_language: The Data Fidu002cciary must give a notice to the Data Principal that tells them what personal information will be used, why it's being used, and how they can exercise their rights and complain if needed.

T6.reviewed_answer: No, targeted advertising aimed at children is not allowed.
T6.reviewed_plain_language: A Data Fiduciary cannot track children or show them targeted ads.

T7.notes: Period to be prescribed by rules.
T7.reviewed_answer: The Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager must respond to grievances within a prescribed period.
T7.reviewed_plain_language: The company has to reply to your grievance within a time frame set by the government rules.

T8.notes: Lists grievance redressal (a right, s.13) as a duty; omits impersonation and false-grievance duties.
T8.reviewed_answer: As a Data Principal, you must comply with all applicable laws, ensure authenticity of information, and have means for grievance redressal.
T8.reviewed_plain_language: You must follow all laws, make sure your personal data is real, and have a way to complain if something goes wrong.

T9.notes: Retrieval missed s.16; model fell back.
T9.reviewed_answer: I don't have information on that. It is not covered in the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

T10.reviewed_answer: You have sixty days to appeal against an order of the Data Protection Board, and the appeal must be filed before the Appellate Tribunal.
T10.reviewed_plain_language: You must appeal within 60 days, and the appeal goes to the Appellate Tribunal.
